name: Antietam
label: Homestead
lede: Tara Key and Tim Harris left Louisville punk for New York, borrowed a name from the Civil War, and have kept Antietam going, with one long gap, for over forty years.

eras.title: Louisville barns, then New York
eras.text: Key and Harris came out of Louisville's first punk wave in 1978, moved to New York in the fall of 1983, and named the new band after the bloodiest day of the Civil War.

yt: Tara Key on WRFL-FM's Trivial Thursdays
years.h: Louisville punk shows up in 1978, in barns and living rooms
years.p: Harris on the year No Fun (Key's band) and Babylon Dance Band (his) started within weeks of each other, alongside the Endtables, the Blinders and the I-Holes.
years.xp:
Harris told LEO Weekly that was how 1978 felt. The bands played barns, galleries and living rooms until the South 40 in Iroquois gave them a room.

Key joined Babylon Dance Band after Harris started it. Chronogram dates the band 1978 to 1983.

years.p: Perfect Sound Forever dates the move to the fall of 1983, months before the band that became Antietam had a name.
years.xp:
Key told Perfect Sound Forever that making the cover of the Village Voice within the first year and a half of "having a band" (Babylon Dance Band) made it easier to "grab the bullhorn."

Sources place them in Hoboken, near Maxwell's, in these years. AllMusic instead says the move came in the late 1980s, which the other accounts contradict.

years.h: A new band takes the Civil War's bloodiest day as its name
years.p: Key and Harris start it on Derby Day 1984 with Wolf Knapp and Michael Weinert.
years.xp:
LEO Weekly puts the founding on Derby Day 1984. Chronogram reports that D. Boon of the Minutemen ribbed them for using the Northern name for the battle, Antietam, when the Southern one, Sharpsburg, was right there.

Wikipedia and Rock and Roll Globe both list Knapp and Weinert in the first lineup; Knapp left after the early recordings.

eras.title: Gerard Cosloy signs them
eras.text: Two records for Cosloy's Homestead label, and a drummer who plays on only one of them.

years.src: The Noise Room · Trouser Press · Wikipedia: Antietam (band)
years.h: Cosloy sees them open for Hüsker Dü and signs them
years.p: Gerard Cosloy catches the band at Maxwell's in Hoboken, per The Noise Room, and Homestead puts out Antietam in July.
years.xp:
The Noise Room says the band's first show was at CBGB and that Cosloy found them at Maxwell's. Trouser Press was lukewarm about the first two records, calling the songs "a bit too inconspicuous, too gentle" and saying Key's guitar was not yet fully on display.

Wikipedia dates the release to July 1985.

years.h: Sean Mulhall drums on Music from Elba and on nothing else
years.p: A Babylon Dance Band alumnus, Mulhall plays on the second Homestead album and on no other Antietam record.
years.xp: An "Until Now / Rain" single also came out on Homestead in 1986. Then the band went quiet for about three years.

eras.title: Yo La Tengo at the board, a 20-year-old on drums
eras.text: A move to Triple X, Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley producing, and Josh Madell behind the kit made the band louder.

years.h: Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley produce Burgoo
years.p: Yo La Tengo's two founders run the board on the band's first Triple X album, with Charles Schultz on drums.
years.xp: A 1989 single, "Eaten Up by Hate" with "Naples" and "Day Before Tomorrow," on Triple X came first. Trouser Press calls Burgoo the point where Key's angular guitar comes forward.

years.src: Rock and Roll Globe · Wikipedia: Antietam (band)
years.h: A 20-year-old named Josh Madell takes the drum stool
years.p: Madell replaces Charles Schultz and is still behind the kit three decades later.
years.xp: Rock and Roll Globe says Madell was 20 when he joined. It names Mike Weinert as the outgoing drummer, while Wikipedia names Schultz.

yt: Live at Lounge Ax, Chicago, Nov. 7, 1991
years.h: Everywhere Outside turns up with Madell on drums
years.p: Trouser Press hears the intensity jump, one year after Burgoo.

years.h: Antietam Comes Alive! puts CBGB on tape
years.p: A live record from the Bowery club, out on Triple X.
years.xp: Trouser Press says it hits "with the room-spinning displacement of a furious tequila buzz."

years.h: Rope-a-Dope goes back to Homestead and closes on 11 minutes
years.p: Lyle Hysen and the band produce. Kaplan plays on "Hands Down" and the band covers Dead Moon's "Graveyard."
years.xp:
AllMusic called it "an unjustly overlooked piece of mid-'90s indie rock," and Guitar Player praised Key's distorted tone. "Silver Solace" is the 11-minute closer.

The same year Key released her solo album Bourbon County on Homestead, followed by Ear and Echo in 1995.

years.h: Key plays the Factory house band in I Shot Andy Warhol
years.p: She appears with Yo La Tengo as the band in the 1996 film; the Antietam single "Alibi" comes out on Other Music the same year.
years.xp: Members kept busy in between: Key made Dark Edson Tiger (1999, Thrill Jockey) with Rick Rizzo of Eleventh Dream Day, Harris played with Yo La Tengo, and Madell drummed in Codeine and Retsin.

eras.title: Back on Carrot Top, then their own label
eras.text: After a ten-year gap between albums, Victory Park came out on Chicago's Carrot Top; in 2017 the band put a record out on its own Motorific Sounds.

years.h: A ten-year gap ends with Victory Park
years.p: The reunion record is the first of three for Chicago's Carrot Top.

years.src: Wikipedia: Opus Mixtum · Perfect Sound Forever
years.h: Opus Mixtum runs two discs, with Rick Rizzo on guitar
years.p: Recorded at Seaside Lounge with Josh Clark; one track covers the Rugbys.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band first imagined an instrumental-only record. Tenth Life followed in 2011, their third for Carrot Top; AllMusic and PSF describe it as poppier.

years.h: Antietam becomes its own label with Intimations of Immortality
years.p: The album comes out on Motorific Sounds, after three records on Carrot Top.

eras.title: Still going
eras.text: Four decades in, there's a new EP, a record on Dromedary, and Madell's daughter Trixie sitting in.

yt: Bowery Ballroom, opening for Yo La Tengo, Jan. 1, 2025
years.h: A four-song EP lands in the band's fortieth year
years.p: LEO Weekly says the band called Pitch & Yaw some of their strongest material.
years.xp: Madell's daughter Trixie performed with the band during Yo La Tengo's 2024 Hanukkah shows, per Magnet.

years.src: Chronogram · Magnet · Into Music · Listen Local
years.h: Album fourteen, The Counting Game, arrives on Dromedary
years.p: It comes out the same weekend the band plays Dromfest in Catskill, New York (September 4-6).
years.xp: The album includes Trixie Madell on "Spy Vs. Spy" and banjo from Steve Cooley. The opener "Way Too Well" is a garage rocker from 1997 that had never been released.
